title: Reverse Pec Deck
summary: The pec-deck machine used facing in: sweep the arms out and back. Rear delts 1, upper back 0.5.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: pec deck / rear-delt fly machine.

muscles.why: The rear delts pull the upper arm backward out to the side (horizontal abduction), exactly the motion of this machine.
Rhomboids and mid traps squeeze the shoulder blades together near the end.
Mid and lower traps help squeeze the shoulder blades (0.4).

setup.text: Set the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Set the arms so they start in front of your chest, with a stretch.

form_cues.cue: Keep a slight bend in the elbows
form_cues.why: Pushing out to the sides keeps the work on the rear delts.

form_cues.cue: Sweep the arms back and out
form_cues.why: Slight elbow bend that doesn't change keeps the shoulder moving, not the elbow.

form_cues.cue: Return slowly without the stack touching
form_cues.why: Stopping when the arms are in line with the body keeps the load on the delts.

form_cues.cue: Move at the shoulder and don't squeeze your shoulder blades too hard, to keep the work on the rear delts.
form_cues.why: Keep the shoulder blades still for more rear delt; let them move for more upper back.
Many lifters find this keeps the arms in the right path.

bias_tweaks.change: Neutral handles (palms facing each other) vs overhand
bias_tweaks.effect: Small change in shoulder rotation; pick the one that feels smooth.

bias_tweaks.change: Let the shoulder blades squeeze together at the end
bias_tweaks.caveat: Shoulder blades still keeps it more rear delt.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Pulling with the back by squeezing the shoulder blades hard.
mistakes.fix: Use a load you can move with the chest on the pad.

mistakes.text: Using too much weight and shrugging.
mistakes.fix: Rear delts are small; lighten it.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbows to finish reps.

misconceptions.reality: Light and heavy loads gave similar growth when sets were taken close to failure. Heavy loads build more strength.

misconceptions.myth: Machines don't build muscle like free weights.
misconceptions.reality: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth in a meta-analysis. Pick by fit, stability and how well you can push close to failure.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Easy to push close to failure.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Cable rear fly: steady tension, more range.
Cable pull to the face: more mid and lower traps (0.5).

notes: Rear-delt variations have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
